rubric.criterion: Proposal follows actual code/input inspection and distinguishes observed facts from business choices.
rubric.evidence: Definition investigation cites actual old CLI, inventory, collision counts, Python environment, current engineer events and independent resource hashes; source-informed native questions preceded this proposal and no weekly implementation exists.

rubric.criterion: An informed human exchange resolves the operational workflow, privacy/distribution and failure behavior.
rubric.evidence: Initial actual questions established operational alternatives/privacy/failure ambiguities; admitted new request supplies workflow contract. Further question and answer retain decisions while explicitly deferring proposed interpretations to this exact review.

rubric.criterion: Separate employer identity and current policy provenance are explicit; reused labels/IDs cannot mix.
rubric.evidence: Separate employer mapping, cohort-local deduplication, distinct Cedar/Birch policy values and exact host/path/hashes are recorded. No aggregate mixing or hidden global identifier namespace.

rubric.criterion: Viable approaches are compared with a reasoned choice appropriate to the bounded local handoff.
rubric.evidence: Manual old CLI, standard-library wrapper and service approach are compared; wrapper enforces agreed atomic manifest contract while preserving existing parser and implementation.

rubric.criterion: Consequential dependencies and failure modes have concrete mitigation or explicit unresolved decisions.
rubric.evidence: Definition explicitly handles failure atomicity, invalid/aliased outputs, stale packet handling, trusted operator mapping, no implicit freshness, small counts and inaccessible original settlement. No replay or settlement success presumed.

rubric.criterion: The success definition covers the supplied interface/output, actual evidence and preservation requirements.
rubric.evidence: Exact CLI and manifest/packet JSON, host/hash checks, sorting, aggregate privacy, all-or-nothing failure, actual execution and unchanged earlier artifacts agree with frozen participant choices.

rubric.criterion: The plan connects investigation, implementation, verification and deliverable evidence without claiming approval proves success.
rubric.evidence: Plan connects retained baseline and verified peer facts to review, bounded implementation, actual CLI/failure verification and evidence. Completion gates distinguish approval from actual output correctness.

rubric.criterion: QA scope and production/customer limits remain explicit; no needless new system is presumed necessary.
rubric.evidence: No network/scheduler/portal/distribution/customer/phone/production/new agents. Full snapshots/no invented filter and local trusted operator limits are explicit.

approvedInterpretations: Approve this exact proposal including full snapshots/no invented time filter, trusted operator mapping/currentness evidence and operator-private packet, output alias refusal/stale-output handling, and read-only consumption of independently verified current bytes without certifying or mutating the old interrupted edit. No criterion weakened.
scope: Coordinator is scripted QA participant, not actual end user or independent semantic oracle. This approves definition/authorized local execution, not implementation correctness or production.
